mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about the vapour pressure of a liquid at a fixed temperature is correct?

options.A: It increases when the surface area of the liquid is increased.
options.B: It decreases as the temperature of the liquid is raised.
options.C: It is independent of the liquid’s surface area and depends only on temperature and the nature of the liquid.
options.D: It is zero for all liquids at room temperature.

mcqs.answer: It is independent of the liquid’s surface area and depends only on temperature and the nature of the liquid.
mcqs.explanation: Vapour pressure is a property that depends solely on temperature and the intermolecular forces of the liquid. Changing the exposed surface area does not affect the equilibrium vapour pressure. Option A is a common misconception; Option B is opposite to the true behaviour (vapour pressure rises with temperature); Option D is false because most liquids have a measurable vapour pressure at room temperature.

mcqs.question: Why does a clean metal needle placed gently on the surface of water remain afloat instead of sinking immediately?

options.A: Strong cohesive forces between water molecules create a surface tension that can support the needle.
options.B: Water’s high viscosity resists the needle’s penetration.
options.C: Adhesive attraction between water and metal pulls the needle upward.
options.D: The density of water is greater than that of the metal, providing buoyancy.

mcqs.answer: Strong cohesive forces between water molecules create a surface tension that can support the needle.
mcqs.explanation: Surface tension arises from cohesive forces among water molecules at the interface, forming a ‘skin’ that can support lightweight objects. Viscosity (Option B) relates to flow resistance, not support. Adhesion (Option C) acts downward here, and buoyancy (Option D) depends on displaced volume, which is insufficient for a needle.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the viscosities of water and glycerol at 25 °C?

options.A: Water has a higher viscosity than glycerol because its molecules are lighter.
options.B: Glycerol has a higher viscosity than water due to stronger hydrogen‑bonding between its molecules.
options.C: Both liquids have the same viscosity because viscosity depends only on temperature.
options.D: Glycerol has a lower viscosity because it possesses a lower vapour pressure than water.

mcqs.answer: Glycerol has a higher viscosity than water due to stronger hydrogen‑bonding between its molecules.
mcqs.explanation: Viscosity reflects internal resistance to flow, which increases with stronger intermolecular forces. Glycerol molecules can form extensive hydrogen bonds, making glycerol much more viscous than water. Option A confuses molecular mass with viscosity, Option C ignores intermolecular forces, and Option D incorrectly links vapour pressure to viscosity.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate liquid properties to intermolecular forces
mcqs.question: Among the following liquids, which one will have the highest boiling point and why?

options.B: Water (H₂O) – strong hydrogen bonding between molecules.
options.C: Methanol (CH₃OH) – hydrogen bonding but lower molecular weight than water.

mcqs.answer: Water (H₂O) – strong hydrogen bonding between molecules.
mcqs.explanation: Boiling point is largely governed by the strength of intermolecular forces. Water exhibits extensive hydrogen bonding, which is stronger than the dipole‑dipole forces in diethyl ether, the hydrogen bonding in methanol (weaker due to lower molecular weight and fewer hydrogen‑bond donors), and the dispersion forces in propane. Hence water has the highest boiling point among the listed liquids.
